actuality.title: News
actuality.description: Based on geological maps of the DRC, your mining permits are placed in their overall and regional geological context. A description of geological, structural, and stratigraphic formations in relation to known mineral indices from geological services and literature is presented to guide your explorations. Geological maps provide essential information about exposed geological layers, such as their lithologies, ages (stratigraphy), structural positions (tectonics), and the location of old and active mines, as well as potential mineral indices.

showcase.title: Our References and Projects
showcase.description: Geophysics is widely used as a direct detection tool for mineral exploration. The contrast between the specific physical properties of ore deposits and their host rock creates 'anomalies' detectable at the surface or from the air. This applies to contrasts in magnetic susceptibility, density, electrical conductivity, and natural radioactivity (Thorium, Uranium, and Potassium). BIGEMIP SARL links these geophysical anomalies with geological formations within your mining permits and can provide qualitative and quantitative (if available) elements of regional or local geological models likely to contain economically viable mineralization.

baseMap.title: BASE GEOLOGICAL MAP
baseMap.description: With its experience in applied geology and geoinformatics, BIGEMIP SARL supports mining sector operators in producing and updating reliable and accurate geological maps that meet international standards.
points: Regional and local geological maps illustrating lithological formations and stratigraphic units.
Structural maps highlighting major tectonic features, folds, and faults.
Metallogenic maps showing the distribution of known mineral substances and potential zones.

geoScientific.title: THEMATIC GEOSCIENTIFIC MAPS
points: Inventory maps of mineral indices and deposits.
Maps of mining and energy infrastructures, facilitating sectoral planning.

mining.title: MINING AND RESOURCE INVENTORY MAPS
points: Hydrogeological maps identifying groundwater and recharge areas.
Geotechnical maps describing the nature and stability of soils for infrastructure works.
Geophysical maps (magnetic, gravimetric, radiometric) for interpreting deep structures.
Regional geochemical maps highlighting trace element anomalies.
Pedological and morpho-structural maps linking geology, relief, and land use.
